name: Emergency Messages
title: Emergency Messages
answer: Emergency messages are pre-written, pre-translated templates for situations like lockdowns, weather closures, or bus delays, drafted with AI help and reviewed by people before any crisis occurs. They matter because during an emergency staff can fill in details instead of writing from scratch, so every family gets accurate information quickly and in their own language.

sections.body: This idea is a set of ready-made message templates for the emergencies a school is most likely to face, such as a lockdown, a weather closure, or a bus delay. AI can help draft the templates and translate them ahead of time, but a person reviews them. The problem it solves is that emergencies demand fast and accurate communication, and writing a message from nothing during a crisis wastes time and invites errors. With templates in hand, staff only fill in the details when something happens. Preparation turns a rushed, improvised task into a short and reliable one.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school, staff prepare templates for the common emergency situations before the year's crises arrive, using AI to draft and translate them with human review. When an emergency actually happens, staff fill in the details rather than writing from scratch, which keeps the message fast and consistent. The text does not give grade bands for this idea, so the practice applies the same way across a school. Translated templates are reviewed by fluent speakers before any emergency occurs, because there will be no time to check a translation during a crisis. Having reviewed templates ready in each major home language means every family receives accurate information at the same time.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or finding for this idea. It presents emergency templates as a matter of preparation and describes the reasoning behind them rather than citing research. The claim that reviewed templates in each major home language ensure accurate information reaches every family at once is stated as the value of preparation, not as a measured result. This idea therefore rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Every emergency message must be approved by an administrator before it is sent, and the text is clear that speed matters but accuracy matters more. A wrong message during an emergency can cause panic or put people in danger, so the approval step is not optional. That step should be quick and clearly assigned so it never becomes a bottleneck. Translated templates must be reviewed by fluent speakers before any emergency occurs, since there will be no time to check a translation during a crisis. The decisions about what a message says and whether it goes out stay with people, not with the AI that helped draft it.
